sentences.en: A psychologist explains why we put off important tasks and how we can break this habit
sentences.zh: 心理学家解释我们为何会推迟做重要的事，以及怎样才能改掉这个习惯。

sentences.en: Procrastination is the habit of delaying a necessary task, usually by focusing on less urgent, more enjoyable, and easier activities instead.
sentences.zh: 拖延是指习惯性地推迟一项必须完成的任务，通常表现为先去做那些没那么紧急、更有趣也更容易的事。

sentences.en: We all do it from time to time.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人偶尔都会这样。

sentences.en: We might be composing a message to a friend who we have to let down, or putting together an important report for college or work; we’re doing our best to avoid doing the job at hand, but deep down we know that we should just be getting on with it.
sentences.zh: 也许我们正要给一个不得不让他失望的朋友写消息，或是要为学业或工作撰写一份重要报告；我们竭力回避眼前的任务，心里却清楚，应该直接动手去做。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, berating ourselves won’t stop us procrastinating again.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，责骂自己并不能阻止我们再次拖延。

sentences.en: In fact, it’s one of the worst things we can do.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这恰恰是我们所能采取的最糟糕的做法之一。

sentences.en: This matters because, as my research shows, procrastination doesn’t just waste time, but is actually linked to other problems, too.
sentences.zh: 这一点很重要，因为我的研究表明，拖延不仅浪费时间，还与其他问题有关。

sentences.en: Contrary to popular belief, procrastination is not due to laziness or poor time management.
sentences.zh: 与普遍看法相反，拖延并非源于懒惰或不善于管理时间。

sentences.en: Scientific studies suggest procrastination is, in fact, caused by poor mood management.
sentences.zh: 科学研究表明，拖延实际上源于不善于调节情绪。

sentences.en: This makes sense if we consider that people are more likely to put off starting or completing tasks that they are really not keen to do.
sentences.zh: 想想就不难理解：遇到自己确实不愿做的任务，人们更可能迟迟不着手，或拖着不做完。

sentences.en: If just thinking about the task threatens our sense of self-worth or makes us anxious, we will be more likely to put it off.
sentences.zh: 如果光是想到某项任务，就会让我们怀疑自己的价值或感到焦虑，我们就更有可能推迟去做。

sentences.en: Research involving brain imaging has found that areas of the brain linked to detection of threats and emotion regulation are actually different in people who chronically procrastinate compared to those who don’t procrastinate frequently.
sentences.zh: 一项运用脑成像技术的研究发现，与威胁识别和情绪调节有关的脑区，在长期拖延者和不常拖延的人身上确实有所不同。

sentences.en: Tasks that are emotionally loaded or difficult, such as preparing for exams, are prime candidates for procrastination.
sentences.zh: 容易引起强烈情绪或难度大的任务，如备考，尤其容易被拖延。

sentences.en: People with low self-esteem are more likely to procrastinate.
sentences.zh: 自尊水平较低的人更容易拖延。

sentences.en: Another group of people who tend to procrastinate are perfectionists, who worry their work will be judged harshly by others.
sentences.zh: 另一些容易拖延的人是完美主义者，他们担心别人会苛刻地评价自己的工作。

sentences.en: We know that if we don’t finish that report or complete those home repairs, then what we did can’t be evaluated.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，无论是那份报告还是家里的那些修缮活，只要我们没有做完，别人就无从评价做得怎么样。

sentences.en: When we avoid such tasks, we also avoid the negative emotions associated with them.
sentences.zh: 回避这类任务，我们也就避开了与之相伴的负面情绪。

sentences.en: This is rewarding, and it conditions us to use procrastination to repair our mood.
sentences.zh: 这种做法让我们得到好处，也使我们逐渐习惯于靠拖延来改善心情。

sentences.en: If we engage in more enjoyable tasks instead, we get another mood boost.
sentences.zh: 如果我们转而去做更愉快的事，心情还会再好一些。

sentences.en: In the long run, however, procrastination isn’t an effective way of managing emotions.
sentences.zh: 不过，从长远看，拖延并不是调节情绪的有效方法。

sentences.en: The ‘mood repair’ we experience is temporary.
sentences.zh: 我们所体验到的这种“情绪好转”只是暂时的。

sentences.en: Afterwards, people tend to be left with a sense of guilt that not only increases their negative mood, but also reinforces their tendency to procrastinate.
sentences.zh: 事后，人们往往会感到内疚。这不仅加重了负面情绪，也强化了他们拖延的倾向。

sentences.en: So why is this such a problem?
sentences.zh: 那么，拖延为什么会成为这么大的问题呢？

sentences.en: When most people think of the costs of procrastination, they think of the toll on productivity.
sentences.zh: 说起拖延的代价，大多数人想到的都是它给效率带来的损失。

sentences.en: For example, studies have shown that procrastination negatively impacts on student performance.
sentences.zh: 例如，研究表明，拖延会对学生的学业表现产生不利影响。

sentences.en: But putting off reading textbooks and writing essays may affect other areas of students’ lives.
sentences.zh: 但迟迟不读课本、不写论文，还可能影响学生生活的其他方面。

sentences.en: In one study of over 3,000 German students over a six-month period, those who reported procrastinating over their university work were also more likely to engage in study-related misconduct, such as cheating and plagiarism.
sentences.zh: 一项为期六个月的研究涉及3000多名德国学生。那些自称会拖延大学课业的学生，也更可能出现作弊、抄袭等学业不端行为。

sentences.en: But the behaviour that procrastination was most closely linked with was using fraudulent excuses to get deadline extensions.
sentences.zh: 不过，与拖延关联最密切的行为，是编造借口来延长提交期限。

sentences.en: Other research shows that employees on average spend almost a quarter of their workday procrastinating, and again this is linked with negative outcomes.
sentences.zh: 另有研究表明，员工平均每天有将近四分之一的工作时间耗在拖延上，这同样与不良后果有关。

sentences.en: In fact, in one US survey of over 22,000 employees, participants who said they regularly procrastinated had less annual income and less employment stability.
sentences.zh: 事实上，美国一项涉及2.2万多名员工的调查发现，自称经常拖延的人年收入较低，工作也较不稳定。

sentences.en: For every one-point increase on a measure of chronic procrastination, annual income decreased by US$15,000.
sentences.zh: 在一项衡量长期拖延程度的指标上，得分每高一分，年收入就少1.5万美元。

sentences.en: Procrastination also correlates with serious health and well-being problems.
sentences.zh: 拖延还与严重影响健康和幸福感的问题有关。

sentences.en: A tendency to procrastinate is linked to poor mental health, including higher levels of depression and anxiety.
sentences.zh: 拖延倾向与较差的心理健康状况有关，包括更严重的抑郁和焦虑。

sentences.en: Across numerous studies, I’ve found people who regularly procrastinate report a greater number of health issues, such as headaches, flu and colds, and digestive issues.
sentences.zh: 我在多项研究中发现，经常拖延的人自述有更多健康问题，如头痛、流感、感冒和消化问题。

sentences.en: They also experience higher levels of stress and poor sleep quality.
sentences.zh: 他们承受的压力也更大，睡眠质量也差。

sentences.en: They are less likely to practise healthy behaviours, such as eating a healthy diet and regularly exercising, and use destructive coping strategies to manage their stress.
sentences.zh: 他们较少采取健康的生活方式，如健康饮食和定期锻炼，还会以有害的方式应对压力。

sentences.en: In one study of over 700 people, I found people prone to procrastination had a 63% greater risk of poor heart health after accounting for other personality traits and demographics.
sentences.zh: 在一项涉及700多人的研究中，我发现容易拖延的人心脏健康状况不佳的风险高出63%；这一结果已考虑到其他性格特征和人口统计因素。

sentences.en: Finding better ways of managing our emotions is one route out of the vicious cycle of procrastination.
sentences.zh: 找到更好的情绪调节方法，是走出拖延恶性循环的一条途径。

sentences.en: An important first step is to manage our environment and how we view the task.
sentences.zh: 重要的第一步，是管理好周围的环境，并调整我们看待任务的方式。

sentences.en: There are a number of evidence-based strategies that can help us fend off distractions that can occupy our minds when we should be focusing on the thing we should be getting on with.
sentences.zh: 我们本应专心做手头的事，却可能被别的事情占据心思。有多种经过实证检验的策略能帮助我们排除这类干扰。

sentences.en: For example, reminding ourselves about why the task is important and valuable can increase positive feelings towards it.
sentences.zh: 例如，提醒自己一项任务为何重要、有何价值，可以让我们对它产生更多积极的感受。

sentences.en: Forgiving ourselves and feeling compassion when we procrastinate can help break the procrastination cycle.
sentences.zh: 拖延时，原谅自己、对自己多一分体谅，有助于打破拖延的循环。

sentences.en: We should admit that we feel bad, but not be overly critical of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们应该承认自己心里不好受，但也不应过分苛责自己。

sentences.en: We should remind ourselves that we’re not the first person to procrastinate, nor the last.
sentences.zh: 我们应该提醒自己：自己并非第一个拖延的人，也不会是最后一个。

sentences.en: Doing this can take the edge off the negative feelings we have about ourselves when we procrastinate.
sentences.zh: 这样做能缓解我们在拖延时对自己产生的负面感受。

sentences.en: This can all make it easier to get back on track.
sentences.zh: 这些做法都能让我们更容易回到正轨上。

questions.question: mention of false assumptions about why people procrastinate
reference to the realisation that others also procrastinate
neurological evidence of a link between procrastination and emotion
Many people think that procrastination is the result of ______
The tasks we are most likely to put off are those that could damage our self-esteem or cause us to feel ______ when we think about them.
differences in the brain regions associated with regulating emotions and identifying ______
Getting ready to take ______ might be a typical example of one such task.
People who are likely to procrastinate tend to be either ______ those with low self-esteem.
It's often followed by a feeling of ______, which worsens our mood and leads to more procrastination.
Which TWO comparisons between employees who often procrastinate and those who do not are mentioned in the text?

options.B: The quality of their work is inferior.
options.C: They don't keep their jobs for as long.
options.D: They don't enjoy their working lives as much.
options.E: They have poorer relationships with colleagues.

questions.logic: 调查比较经常拖延与不经常拖延的雇员。less annual income 对应 A，即经常拖延者年收入较低；less employment stability 对应 C，即工作较不稳定。这是调查发现的群体差异，单凭它不能判定某位雇员离职的原因。

questions.question: Which TWO recommendations for getting out of a cycle of procrastination does the writer give?

options.D: prioritising tasks according to their importance
options.E: avoiding things that stop us concentrating on our tasks

questions.logic: E 对应 fend off distractions，排除让自己无法专注于任务的干扰。A 对应 not be overly critical，承认自己因拖延而难受，同时给自己一些宽容。文中让人回想任务的价值，没有要求按重要程度给任务排序。
